transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my eating has gotten really out of control, especially at night. Like, I’ll come home after teaching and grading papers, and I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, but then somehow it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter… whatever snacks I had packed for my classroom.

It’s embarrassing to say, because I’m usually the one telling kids to make good choices, and then I’m at home eating this amount of food that honestly scares me.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate or control your weight?

I don’t usually, um… make myself throw up or anything like that. But I do try to “make up for it,” I guess. Like after one of those nights, I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school, which is ridiculous because I’m around kids all day and I’m supposed to be, you know, functioning.

And then after work I’ll go out on the trail and stay there for hours, or I’ll do extra yoga even when I’m shaky and exhausted. Sometimes I tell myself it’s just because I need to clear my head, like teaching can be so loud and chaotic, especially after indoor recess days… but honestly, it’s mostly because I feel like I have to undo what I did.
During these episodes when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you can't stop yourself or control what or how much you're eating?

Yeah… yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most. Once I start, it’s like the reasonable teacher part of me is watching from outside my body saying, “Joan, stop, what are you doing?” but my hands just keep opening things and putting food in my mouth.

It’s weird, because in my classroom I can be so organized—like I have color-coded bins and a whole system for missing pencils, which is ridiculous but necessary—and then at home it’s like none of that control exists. I’ll keep going until I’m painfully full, even if I don’t actually want any more.
Can you recall how often these episodes happen—like, how many times a week or month you feel like you lose control and can't stop eating once you start?

It’s… it’s been pretty regular, unfortunately. I used to tell myself it was just a bad day here or there, like after parent-teacher conferences or when my lesson plans got thrown off, but for the past few months I don’t think there’s really been many weeks where it didn’t happen at least once.

Usually it’s one night where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I’m in this whole punishment mode, like I won’t eat at school or I’ll make myself do this really long walk or extra yoga even if I’m tired. So… yeah, at least weekly, I guess.
Do these eating episodes and the way you feel about them cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your work, relationships, or daily life?

Yeah… it does. More than I like admitting.

I’ll think, “Okay, tonight I need to grade those spelling tests,” or call my friend back, or even just do laundry, and then the whole evening turns into… trying to undo what happened with food. Like planning around a long walk or yoga or not eating enough the next day, and then I’m exhausted and behind on everything.

And weekends too, which is embarrassing because teachers talk about weekends like they’re for catching up and seeing people, and mine end up getting organized around whether I messed up with food. I’ve been slower getting grading done, and when I’m with friends I’m not really there, I’m half thinking about food or what I’m going to do later to make up for it.

At work I try really hard to seem put-together. I mean, I have to—twenty-something kids are looking at me like I know what I’m doing, and I’m supposed to be the calm adult with the sticker chart and the clean whiteboard. But inside I’m constantly worried people can tell I’m not okay. So yes, it’s interfering. I’m still functioning, but it takes up so much space.
Can you describe what it feels like in the moment when you're eating—do you feel like you're choosing to eat each time, or does it feel like something else is in control?

It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing in the normal way, no. I mean, technically I know I’m the one doing it, but in the moment it’s like… the sensible part of me is somewhere outside my body watching it happen.

Like the teacher version of me—the one who can get a whole room of kids to line up quietly, sometimes, on a good day—she’s saying, Joan, stop. You don’t even want this anymore. But my hands just keep going. Opening another thing, taking another bite, almost automatically.

And then I’ll be so full it hurts, and I still feel like I only stopped because my body kind of forced me to, not because I calmly decided to. It’s really scary, actually.
Do these episodes usually happen after a stressful or emotional day, like after a hard time at school or when you're feeling down or anxious?

I… I don’t know if I’ve tracked it that clearly. Sometimes I think it’s after a stressful school day, but then school is stressful a lot, so I’m not sure if that actually means anything.

Like, there are days where a parent email will totally throw me off, or the kids are wild because it rained and they couldn’t go outside, and then I come home feeling kind of wired. But other times it feels like it just happens on a regular night, and then I start trying to find a reason afterward, like maybe I was anxious or tired or whatever.

So… maybe? But I can’t honestly say there’s one clear pattern. I haven’t really been paying attention in that organized of a way.
Can you tell me if these nighttime eating episodes ever happen when you're not really hungry, or if you're already full but still feel like you have to keep eating?

Yes… that definitely happens. A lot of the time I’m not even really hungry by the point it keeps going. It’s more like once I start, something switches.

I’ll be standing in the kitchen, or sitting there with whatever it is, and the reasonable part of me—the teacher part that can tell a whole class, “Okay, pencils down, eyes up here”—is sort of watching from outside saying, Joan, stop. You’re full. You don’t need more. And then my hands just… keep opening things. Keep putting food in my mouth.

It’s weird because I’ll even feel painfully full, like uncomfortable full, and I still don’t feel like I can just decide to stop. I mean, I can make twenty-seven kids put their folders in the right bin, but I can’t make myself stop eating crackers or cereal or whatever, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud. But yes, it happens when I’m not hungry, and even when I’m already full.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really timed it or noticed the speed exactly. I mean, it probably isn’t like sitting down to a normal dinner, where I’m using a plate and pretending to be civilized and all that.

Sometimes I’m just sort of… standing there, and things are happening quickly because I’m not really thinking through each bite. But I don’t know if I’d say “much more quickly” for sure. It’s funny, with my students I notice every tiny thing—who’s rushing through their work, who’s taking forever to write one sentence—but with myself during this, it’s like I’m not observing it clearly.

So… maybe? I just haven’t paid attention to the pace as much as the fact that it’s happening.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you’re embarrassed about how much you’re eating or what you’re eating?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’m usually alone at night anyway, so it’s not like I’m making some big plan to hide, if that makes sense.

I don’t think I’ve really sorted out whether it’s because I’m embarrassed or just because that’s when I’m by myself. I live my whole day in front of people—kids asking questions, coworkers popping in, someone needing glue sticks or a behavior chart or whatever—so by the time I’m home, being alone just kind of happens.

But… I guess I also wouldn’t want someone standing there watching me. That would feel awful. I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking. I haven’t really thought about the “why” of being alone, exactly.
Can you recall if you feel like you have no control over your eating during these episodes, like you can’t stop eating even if you want to?

Yes. That’s probably the main thing, honestly—the no-control part.

It’s like once I start, the sensible part of me is still there, sort of hovering off to the side. Like the teacher voice in my head is going, Joan, stop. Enough. You’re full. And I can hear it, the same way I can hear myself telling kids to line up quietly or not sharpen pencils during a lesson—sorry, that’s such a teacher example, but that’s what it feels like.

But my body doesn’t listen. My hands just keep opening things, keep putting food in my mouth, and I’m thinking I should stop, I want to stop, and then somehow I’m still doing it. Even when I’m so full it hurts. It feels really… humiliating, I guess, because I can manage a classroom, but in those moments I can’t seem to manage myself.
